workflow_runs.display_title: Give the Kotlin compile daemon enough heap to read material-icons-ext…

head_commit.message:
Give the Kotlin compile daemon enough heap to read material-icons-extended

The release build's :app:compileReleaseKotlin failed with
"Not enough memory to run compilation" on the shared runner while the K2
compiler streamed material-icons-extended-release-api.jar through ASM to
resolve SendAndArchiveKt for PlaylistDetailScreen.kt:504. The daemon's
default 1.5 GB was not enough for that container on a constrained host.

gradle.properties sized kotlin.daemon.jvmargs for small local boxes
(-Xmx1280m), which is fine for a developer machine with a private daemon but
starves on the shared runner where the daemon has to compete with AAPT2, D8
and R8 for the same host. Raise it to 2 GB with a matching metaspace.

Verified locally: `:app:compileReleaseKotlin` with the new setting completes
in 3m 15s, including the call site that previously OOM'd.

The signing secret slots accept two names each, so reporting only one could

workflow_runs.name: Publish Selected Release
workflow_runs.display_title: Surface release build failures as step annotations

head_commit.message:
Surface release build failures as step annotations

A red release build was only actionable to someone who could open the run in a
browser and expand the step log. Downloading a job log over the API requires
repo admin, so tooling and automation saw nothing but "Process completed with
exit code 1" and could not tell a configuration-time validation error from a
native compile failure.

Capture the Gradle output and re-emit the lines that identify the cause -- the
first Kotlin/C++ error, the failed task, and the "What went wrong" block -- as
annotations, which are readable from the public check-runs API. The build's exit
status is preserved, so this only adds diagnostics and never turns a failing
build into a passing one.

workflow_runs.display_title: Stop generateNativeSecrets failing on CI when .env is absent

head_commit.message:
Stop generateNativeSecrets failing on CI when .env is absent

.env is gitignored, so it exists on developer machines but never on a runner.
Gradle 9 validates a missing inputs.file(...) target even when .optional() was
called, so every release build died at configuration time with "specifies file
'.env' which doesn't exist" -- the cause of the red build.yml runs on main, and
unrelated to the updater.

Track the file's presence as a property and only declare it as an input when it
is actually there. Up-to-date behaviour is unchanged: a developer editing .env
still re-runs the task, and a runner without one records a stable false.

workflow_runs.name: Publish Selected Release
workflow_runs.display_title: Trigger releases from tag pushes, not just manual dispatch

head_commit.message:
Trigger releases from tag pushes, not just manual dispatch

Publishing a release was a manual step: bump the version, then remember to run
the workflow by hand against the tag. That is the step most likely to be
skipped or mistyped, and the verify gate turns a mistyped tag into a red build
after the tag already exists.

Pushing a v* tag now builds and publishes on its own. workflow_dispatch stays as
the escape hatch for re-publishing an existing tag with custom notes or
recovering a failed publish. inputs.* is empty on a tag push, so the concurrency
group, the tag resolution in verify, and the publish step each fall back to the
ref or to the tag verify resolved -- otherwise the run would have failed at
'cannot resolve release ref' with no input to read. The title falls back to
Bhavyam <versionName>, and an empty release_notes now means the package notice
alone rather than a required input.

workflow_runs.name: Build Bhavyam APK
workflow_runs.display_title: Add in-app update download and install, order releases by publish dat…

head_commit.message:
Add in-app update download and install, order releases by publish date, bump to 1.1

Detect new GitHub releases on a 6h-throttled foreground check, download the
release APK through DownloadManager, verify its signing cert and versionCode,
then hand it to the system installer. Falls back to the browser when a release
ships no .apk asset or the APK cannot be installed.

Update ordering now keys on the release publish date rather than the version
string, so the scheme can be renumbered (4.2.2 -> 1.1) without stranding
installs already on a higher-looking version. The version only needs to differ
from ours, which also stops a fresh install of the newest build being offered
its own update.

Also gate the Liquid Glass switch on device capability so it cannot read ON
while every call site takes its fallback path, and clear the remaining
compiler warnings in the settings UI.

workflow_runs.display_title: Remove unused launcher/widget drawables, brand assets and build logs

head_commit.message:
Remove unused launcher/widget drawables, brand assets and build logs

The five drawables removed here were already unreferenced: widget_background,
widget_circle, widget_pill_bg and widget_play_pill were superseded by the
widget_ref_* family, and ic_launcher_logo was orphaned. The adaptive icon
resolves ic_launcher_adaptive_bg, ic_launcher_foreground and
ic_launcher_monochrome, all of which remain. The root-level bhavya.png,
bhavya_logo.png and bhavya_logo.svg were unreferenced (README uses
bhavyam.png) and the committed build_log.txt and run_log*.txt are build
output. Also corrects the ic_launcher_background comment in colors.xml.
